title: Fugaro decision agent answer
description: What one decision call answers with, handed to `claude -p` as `--json-schema` and read back by internal/orchestrator/decide.ParseAnswer (the stateless-orchestrator plan's O12). It is the model's own contract with the daemon and it is closed: the answer is decoded strictly, so a field this release does not model is refused rather than dropped, and an answer that carries one never lands. The document is not a permission — nothing here decides what an op may do. The ops are decoded as orchestrator.Op (schemas/orchestrator-patch.schema.json's own shape, which is why they are asked for as opaque objects here) and applied by code through orchestrator.Apply under the DecisionAgent class, which refuses every op that class may not make: an approval, the goal, a question that waits on a person, a phase, a run id, an attempt or an intent. There is deliberately no field naming a model or a class: the model comes from the changed paths through O1's classifier and O4's policy key, and an answer that could name one would be a second place that rule lives. internal/orchestrator/decide.OutputSchema is the same document on one line, which is what the flag takes, and TestOutputSchemaMatchesTheSchemaFile is what keeps the two one thing.

reasoning.$comment: What the model decided and why, as a person reads it later in the audit log (internal/orchestrator/decide.Runner.audit). An empty one is refused: a decision nobody can read the reason for is a decision a person cannot review.

items.$comment: One orchestrator.Op, decoded strictly and validated against the actor's class. An empty list is refused (decide.ErrNoDecision): a cycle that asked a model and changed nothing is the same cycle as one that failed, and the breaker is what a person sees when it happens three times in a row (G10).
